question: Should this PR land the broad Codex Computer Use defaults, cache reconciliation, periodic health/repair, fallback policy, lease manager, and direct MCP probe exception as one change, or should it be narrowed before merge?
rationale: The patch changes setup/startup defaults, config contract, filesystem cache behavior, host process cleanup, and a sandbox-adjacent MCP boundary; those are maintainer product and security-boundary choices beyond a mechanical readiness bug fix.

options.title: Narrow Before Merge
options.body: Keep the live readiness and cache repair path, but defer or remove broader defaults until the MCP exception, repair behavior, health cadence, and lease surface are owner-approved separately.

options.title: Accept Broad Defaults
options.body: Maintainers can intentionally accept the compatibility and security-boundary changes as product direction, relying on the included live macOS proof and exact-head CI before merge.

options.title: Split The Branch
options.body: Ask for smaller PRs for cache reconciliation, readiness probing, health monitoring, leases, and docs/config if this combined surface is too broad to review safely.

recommendation.title: Narrow Before Merge
recommendation.body: Keep the live readiness and cache repair path, but defer or remove broader defaults until the MCP exception, repair behavior, health cadence, and lease surface are owner-approved separately.

likelyOwner.reason: kevinslin has recent adjacent ownership history for Codex plugin config, remote app-server plugins, and approval/default behavior.
